questions.q: Why does Marcus Ibe's team build a data landscape inventory before assigning owners or writing quality rules?
options: You can't assign an owner or a rule to a system or column that hasn't been identified and documented first
It is a regulatory requirement with a fixed legal deadline
It is purely a formality with no bearing on later steps
Quality rules must always be written before any inventory exists
questions.explain: A landscape inventory names what exists before any ownership, rule, or classification work can meaningfully attach to it.

questions.q: Which three LTV Global systems each hold an independent, unreconciled 'customer' record per the landscape inventory?
options: Atlas, Beacon, and Comet
Harbor, Summit, and Atlas
Beacon, Harbor, and Summit
Only Summit holds customer data
questions.explain: The inventory shows Atlas (ERP), Beacon (CRM), and Comet (e-commerce) each maintaining their own separate customer record today.

questions.q: What did the landscape review find about Summit, the intended governed analytics layer?
options: It is the least mature system in the inventory, governing almost nothing yet despite its intended role
It is already the single, fully governed source of truth for all domains
It does not appear anywhere in the inventory
It only holds warehouse inventory data
questions.explain: Despite being meant to be the trustworthy, cataloged layer, Summit holds only a handful of ungoverned extracts today — a common, not special, finding.

questions.q: What four questions does the inventory answer for each system?
options: Type, hosting, data domains, and current role versus intended role
Revenue, headcount, founding date, and stock price
Color scheme, logo, slogan, and office location
Password policy, uptime percentage, and vendor contract length
questions.explain: The lesson's inventory table is built from exactly these four columns per system.

questions.q: What is a 'data domain' as used in this lesson's inventory?
options: A logical grouping of related data, such as Customer, Product, or Order
A physical server rack location
A single column in a single table
A company's internet domain name
questions.explain: The Key terms section defines a data domain as a logical grouping of related data, which is how the inventory table organizes each system's contents.
